row.team_price_text: Standard: $10 first full platform user, $99/additional user per month (max 5)
row.evidence: New Relic's automated user management (SCIM) docs say it 'Requires Pro or Enterprise edition', while the pricing page lists SAML single sign-on on Standard; Pro full platform users are $349/user (for annual commitments).
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated). Usage-based pricing (data ingest plus users); SCIM needs Pro ($349 per full platform user/month on annual commitment, $418.80 pay-as-you-go) or Enterprise (Contact Sales), and requires SAML SSO on the authentication domain. SAML SSO alone is on Standard (paid edition, max 5 full platform users: $10 first user, $99 each additional, monthly pay-as-you-go), so the team and SSO per-user price uses the $99 additional-user price (monthly; Standard has no annual price), giving a 3.5x multiplier that June left null. Basic users are free and core users $49 on every paid edition. SCIM 2.0 endpoint at https://scim-provisioning.service.newrelic.com/scim/v2 with a per-authentication-domain bearer token; dedicated New Relic by organization apps exist for Okta, Entra ID and OneLogin.

auth.token_source: Administration > Authentication domains: token shown once when SCIM is enabled for the authentication domain

endpoints.notes: Docs list Group, User, Service provider config, Resource type and Schema; Bulk and Search are not supported.

operations.notes: Deactivate/reactivate via the required 'active' boolean; PUT is partial.

deprovision.notes: IdP apps deactivate (active=false); DELETE /scim/v2/Users/{id} removes the user from the authentication domain. IdP 'suspended' state is unsupported and stays billable (c11).

custom.how: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:newrelic:2.0:User with nrUserType (Full User, Core User, Basic User); other fields are ignored

roles.how: IdP groups are synced; roles and account access are granted to those groups on the New Relic side. User type (basic/core/full) can be set via the nrUserType extension.

limitations.text: Once an authentication domain is set to SCIM, users and groups can't be managed in the UI and the domain can't be changed back.
IdP 'suspended' state is not supported; such users stay billable and keep their user API key.
Bulk and Search endpoints are not supported; filtering is eq-only.
OneLogin cannot delete groups already sent to New Relic.
Users provisioned via SCIM start as basic users unless nrUserType is sent.

auth.notes: Caller must be a core or full platform user with the Authentication Domain Manager role.

capabilities.notes: assign_licenses = user type (FULL_USER_TIER/CORE_USER_TIER/BASIC_USER_TIER) on create/update; assign_roles via authorizationManagementGrantAccess on groups. Delete works only in manually provisioned authentication domains.

endpoints.purpose: Delete a user (manual auth domains only)
Grant a group a role on accounts

limitations.text: User queries return at most 500 users per page (cursor pagination).
userManagementDeleteUser only works in authentication domains set for manually provisioned users.

user_api.notes: Editable authentication domains themselves require Pro or Enterprise (c12 page); NerdGraph is reachable from any account with a user key.

okta.notes: OIN 'New Relic by organization' ticks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push, Group Linking (page markup). A separate 'New Relic by account' app is the legacy model, and an Aquera-built provisioning connector is also listed.

onelogin.notes: From New Relic's OneLogin guide; OneLogin connector page not loaded.
